passages.text: “Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He asks about the life of man.
Man lives on earth.
Man must work hard.
Man’s life is full of labor.
A man’s days are like the days of a hired worker.
A hired worker works for his wages.
A man’s time is filled with toil, like a servant’s.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ צָבָ֣א לֶאֱנ֣וֹשׁ עַל אָ֑רֶץ וְכִימֵ֖י שָׂכִ֣יר יָמָֽיו׃

passages.text: Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.
passages.sermon: A slave longs for shade.\r\nA hired worker waits for his wages.
passages.original: כְּעֶ֥בֶד יִשְׁאַף־ צֵ֑ל וּ֝כְשָׂכִ֗יר יְקַוֶּ֥ה פָעֳלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
God allows Job to experience much pain and loss.
Job says, “I receive months that are empty and useless.”
He says, “Nights full of misery are given to me.”
Job feels that his suffering lasts a long time.
He believes his pain is not by chance, but given to him.
passages.original: כֵּ֤ן הָנְחַ֣לְתִּי לִ֭י יַרְחֵי־ שָׁ֑וְא וְלֵיל֥וֹת עָ֝מָ֗ל מִנּוּ־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He lies down to sleep.
He asks himself, “When will I get up?”
He waits for the evening to end.
He cannot rest.
He tosses and turns all night.
He does not sleep until dawn.
passages.original: אִם־ שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מָתַ֣י אָ֭קוּם וּמִדַּד־ עָ֑רֶב וְשָׂבַ֖עְתִּי נְדֻדִ֣ים עֲדֵי־ נָֽשֶׁף׃

passages.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and encrusted with dirt; my skin is cracked and festering.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his suffering.
His body is sick.
Worms cover his flesh.
Dirt sticks to his skin.
His skin is cracked.
His skin is festering.
passages.original: לָ֘בַ֤שׁ בְּשָׂרִ֣י רִ֭מָּה וְגִישׁ עָפָ֑ר עוֹרִ֥י רָ֝גַ֗ע וַיִּמָּאֵֽס׃

passages.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is suffering.
Job says his days pass very quickly.
His days move faster than a weaver’s shuttle.
His days end.
He has no hope.
passages.original: יָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־ אָ֑רֶג וַ֝יִּכְל֗וּ בְּאֶ֣פֶס תִּקְוָֽה׃

passages.text: Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep suffering.
He feels weak and hopeless.
He says, “My life is only a breath.”
He knows life is short and fragile.
He says, “My eyes will not see good again.”
He believes he will not experience happiness anymore.
passages.original: זְ֭כֹר כִּי־ ר֣וּחַ חַיָּ֑י לֹא־ תָשׁ֥וּב עֵ֝ינִ֗י לִרְא֥וֹת טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.
passages.sermon: Job speaks about his life and coming death.\r\nHe says, “The person who sees me now will not see me again.”\r\nHe says, “You will look at me, but I will not be there.”
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תְ֭שׁוּרֵנִי עֵ֣ין רֹ֑אִי עֵינֶ֖יךָ בִּ֣י וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃

passages.text: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
passages.sermon:
A cloud disappears.
The cloud is gone.
A person goes down to Sheol.
Sheol is the place of the dead.
That person does not return.
He does not come back up.
passages.original: כָּלָ֣ה עָ֭נָן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ כֵּ֥ן יוֹרֵ֥ד שְׁ֝א֗וֹל לֹ֣א יַעֲלֶֽה׃

passages.text: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
passages.sermon: A person who dies does not return to his house.\r\nHis home does not recognize him anymore.\r\nHis place does not remember him.
passages.original: לֹא־ יָשׁ֣וּב ע֣וֹד לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹא־ יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He feels deep pain in his spirit.
He will not keep silent.
He will speak because his spirit is in anguish.
He will complain because his soul is bitter.
passages.original: גַּם־ אֲנִי֮ לֹ֤א אֶחֱשָׂ֫ךְ פִּ֥י אֲ‍ֽ֭דַבְּרָה בְּצַ֣ר רוּחִ֑י אָ֝שִׂ֗יחָה בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels watched and guarded by God.
Job asks, "Am I the sea?"
Job asks, "Am I the monster of the deep?"
Job wonders why God keeps him under guard.
Job is not a dangerous force like the sea.
Job is not a monster that needs to be restrained.
Job questions why God treats him as if he is a threat.
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽיָם־ אָ֭נִי אִם־ תַּנִּ֑ין כִּֽי־ תָשִׂ֖ים עָלַ֣י מִשְׁמָֽר׃

passages.text: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint, then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions, so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He speaks about his pain.
He says, “I think my bed will comfort me.
I hope my couch will ease my complaint.
But You, God, frighten me with dreams.
You terrify me with visions.
I would rather be strangled than live like this.
I prefer death over my life in this body.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אָ֭מַרְתִּי תְּנַחֲמֵ֣נִי עַרְשִׂ֑י יִשָּׂ֥א בְ֝שִׂיחִ֗י מִשְׁכָּבִֽי׃ וְחִתַּתַּ֥נִי בַחֲלֹמ֑וֹת וּֽמֵחֶזְיֹנ֥וֹת תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃ וַתִּבְחַ֣ר מַחֲנָ֣ק נַפְשִׁ֑י מָ֝֗וֶת מֵֽעַצְמוֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks.
Job feels deep sorrow.
Job hates his life.
Job does not want to live forever.
Job asks God to leave him alone.
Job says his days are short.
Job says his life is only a breath.
passages.original: מָ֭אַסְתִּי לֹא־ לְעֹלָ֣ם אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה חֲדַ֥ל מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי כִּי־ הֶ֥בֶל יָמָֽי׃

passages.text: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him, that You attend to him every morning, and test him every moment?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job is a suffering man.
Job asks about mankind.
He says, “What is man?”
He asks, “Why do You make man important?”
He asks, “Why do You care about man?”
He says, “You watch man every morning.”
He says, “You test man every moment.”
passages.original: מָֽה־ אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי־ תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ׃ וַתִּפְקְדֶ֥נּוּ לִבְקָרִ֑ים לִ֝רְגָעִ֗ים תִּבְחָנֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?
passages.sermon:
God, You watch over me constantly.
You do not turn Your gaze away from me.
You do not leave me alone.
You do not give me even a moment’s rest.
You do not let me be, even for the time it takes to swallow my spit.
passages.original: כַּ֭מָּה לֹא־ תִשְׁעֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי לֹֽא־ תַ֝רְפֵּ֗נִי עַד־ בִּלְעִ֥י רֻקִּֽי׃

passages.text: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You ?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job calls God the watcher of mankind.
Job says, “If I have sinned, what have I done to You?”
Job asks God, “Why have You made me Your target?”
Job says, “I have become a burden to You.”
passages.original: חָטָ֡אתִי מָ֤ה אֶפְעַ֨ל׀ לָךְ֮ נֹצֵ֪ר הָאָ֫דָ֥ם לָ֤מָה שַׂמְתַּ֣נִי לְמִפְגָּ֣ע לָ֑ךְ וָאֶהְיֶ֖ה עָלַ֣י לְמַשָּֽׂא׃

passages.text: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels deep sorrow and confusion.
Job asks God a question.
Job says, “Why do You not forgive my sin?”
Job says, “Why do You not remove my guilt?”
Job knows his life is short.
Job says, “Soon I will lie down in the dust.”
Job says, “You will look for me.”
Job says, “I will not be there.”
passages.original: וּמֶ֤ה׀ לֹא־ תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ וְתַעֲבִ֪יר אֶת־ עֲוֺ֫נִ֥י כִּֽי־ עַ֭תָּה לֶעָפָ֣ר אֶשְׁכָּ֑ב וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃פ
